questions.title: HTML5 validation attributes
questions.prompt:
Using JavaScript (not by editing the HTML), turn on HTML5 validation for the form's fields:

- `#email`: make it **required** and change its `type` to `email`
- `#age`: change its `type` to `number` and give it a `min` of 18 and `max` of 120
- `#zip`: give it a `pattern` that allows exactly **5 digits**

The browser then checks these when the form is submitted.

setup.css: body { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; padding: 1em; }

hints: element.pattern = "\\d{5}" — the browser anchors the pattern to the whole value.

tests.name: Email is required and of type email
Age must be 18–120
Zip must be 5 digits

questions.title: checkValidity() and validationMessage
questions.prompt: The form uses HTML5 attributes. Turn off the browser's own error bubbles by setting the form's `noValidate` property to `true`, then handle validation yourself: on `submit`, if `form.checkValidity()` is false, cancel the submit and put each invalid field's `validationMessage` into the `<span>` after it (empty for valid fields).

setup.css:
body { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; padding: 1em; }
span { color: #c0392b; }

hints: for (const field of form.elements) { if (field.tagName === "INPUT") field.nextElementSibling... }
field.validationMessage is "" when the field is valid. Note: the span follows the label here, so use field.parentElement.nextElementSibling.

tests.name: Empty form is cancelled and shows messages
Valid form submits with empty messages

questions.title: setCustomValidity()
questions.prompt: Whenever the user types in `#confirm` (the `input` event), compare it with `#password`. If they differ, call `setCustomValidity("Passwords must match.")` on `#confirm`; if they match, clear the custom message with `setCustomValidity("")`.

setup.css: body { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; padding: 1em; }

hints: A non-empty custom message makes the field invalid; an empty string makes it valid again.

tests.name: A mismatch is invalid with the message
A match is valid

questions.title: jQuery form selectors
questions.prompt:
Using jQuery's form selectors, store:

- `textCount` — the number of text boxes (`:text`)
- `checkedValues` — an **array** of the values of the checked check boxes (`:checkbox:checked`)
- `disabledCount` — the number of disabled controls (`:disabled`)

setup.html:
<form>
  <input type="text" id="first"> <input type="text" id="last"> <input type="text" id="old" disabled>
  <label><input type="checkbox" value="news" checked> News</label>
  <label><input type="checkbox" value="offers"> Offers</label>
  <label><input type="checkbox" value="tips" checked> Tips</label>
  <button disabled>Send</button>
</form>
setup.css: body { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; padding: 1em; }

hints: $(":checkbox:checked").map((i, el) => el.value).get() returns a plain array.

questions.title: focus and blur events
questions.prompt:
For every text box in `#profile`:

- On `focus`, add the class `active`.
- On `blur`, remove the class `active`, trim the value, and if it's empty put `Required` in the `<span>` after it (otherwise empty the span).

tests.name: blur on an empty box removes "active" and shows Required
blur with a value trims it and clears the message

questions.title: Enable a button with change
questions.prompt: The **Submit** button starts disabled. When the `#agree` check box changes, enable the button if it's checked and disable it if not, using jQuery's `prop()` method.

setup.html:
<label><input type="checkbox" id="agree"> I agree</label>
<button id="submit" disabled>Submit</button>
setup.css: body { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; padding: 1em; }

questions.title: Validation application
questions.prompt:
Like the chapter's Validation application: on submit, validate and show messages in each field's following `<span>`:

- `#name`: required → `This field is required.`
- `#age`: a whole number from 18 to 120 → `Enter an age from 18 to 120.`
- `#phone`: matches `999-999-9999` → `Use 999-999-9999 format.`

Clear the message for valid fields, and cancel the submit if any field is invalid.
hints: parseInt the age and check isNaN and the range.

tests.name: Empty form shows three messages and cancels
tests.code:
const ok = document.getElementById("account").dispatchEvent(new Event("submit", { cancelable: true }));
return ok === false && $("#name").next().text() === "This field is required." && $("#age").next().text() === "Enter an age from 18 to 120." && $("#phone").next().text() === "Use 999-999-9999 format.";

tests.name: Age 17 and a bad phone are rejected
Valid data submits

questions.title: Validate as the user types
questions.prompt:
As the user types in `#username` (the `input` event), show the rule that's broken in `#hint`, checking in this order:

1. fewer than 4 characters → `At least 4 characters`
2. contains anything other than letters and digits → `Letters and digits only`
3. otherwise → `Looks good!` and add the class `ok` to `#hint` (remove `ok` in the other cases).
